speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what is the Ministry's rationale in introducing fee benchmarks for medical procedures; (b) how is this new guideline aligned to the spirit of fair competition; and (c) whether the Ministry is aware that the benchmarks may cause doctors who are charging lower fees to charge higher fees.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: asked the Minister for Health whether the removal of the Singapore Medical Association fee benchmarks in 2007 has led to the inflation of medical costs in the last decade and how will the Ministry's fee benchmarks be independently derived so as to prevent anti-competitive price-fixing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This is a shared responsibility and requires a collective effort from all stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We, as individuals, have to take good care of our health and make informed choices when we seek treatment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Healthcare professionals play a key role in providing quality care that is appropriate to patients' needs and charge reasonable fees for their services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Government and healthcare institutions need to continue to improve productivity and look for ways to deliver greater value for patients.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Employers and insurers can help to manage increases in healthcare costs by encouraging prudent use of healthcare services by their employees and policyholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Over the past years, the Ministry of Health (MOH) has been publishing historical transacted hospital bill sizes and operation fees for common medical procedures to enhance transparency of healthcare charges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The introduction of fee benchmarks will take this further by providing all stakeholders a useful reference.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We believe this will encourage appropriate charging practices and provide useful information for patients and payors to make better informed decisions on their care options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The benchmarks will be reviewed and updated regularly, with references made to historical transacted data.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The fee benchmarks serve as references for the public, including insurers and professional bodies, to assess whether the fees charged by a healthcare professional are reasonable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Ministry will, however, continue to monitor the charging practices in the healthcare sector.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Do they include the total bill, with breakdown into the components, such as the doctors' fees and facility fees?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Part of the public concerns have to do with the facility fees charged by the hospitals, which have been increasing quite a fair bit recently.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: The second clarification is on my last question asking whether these benchmarks will cause doctors who are charging lower fees now, to up their fees instead.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: So, we are worried that there could be a knee-jerk reaction.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Indeed, the concern about healthcare fees is not only about doctors' fees.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, this will include doctors' fees, but it would also include facility fees and other components of the overall healthcare cost that patients, insurers, taxpayers and Government, on the whole, will have to pay.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We focused on doctors' fees for a start because these were also the recommendations of the Health Insurance Task Force.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It made a report and recommended that fee benchmarks focused on professional fees in the first instance.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For other fees, such as hospital charges, Dr Lim Wee Kiak is aware that we currently publish the facility fees for common procedures.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If there are ways that we can present the information better to allow members of public and patients to have more information to make comparisons, we would be happy to receive feedback on how we can do better.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We will also continue to monitor if benchmarks for other healthcare-related services will be required in the future.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I mentioned in my reply that we also need collective effort from all stakeholders as providers and institutions need to focus on improving productivity, improving appropriate care.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Recently, we set up the Agency of Care Effectiveness (ACE) and they issued some guidance on appropriate care guides, drug guidances.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These are ways to help medical professionals, patients and caregivers to identify what are the cost-effective treatment options.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, ACE will also be looking into medical technology guidance this year to guide the selection of clinical and cost-effective medical devices.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I am presuming he was also answering Question No 13.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I meant to ask for Mr Deputy Speaker's permission to answer both Question Nos 12 and 13 together.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: First, what other sources of information or expertise would the Ministry be using to ensure the independence of the benchmarks other than that of the Advisory Committee?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Second, how would the Committee be involving the patients because they are not organised into associations or any other kind of bodies?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We want to be able to reflect different perspectives as we set the benchmarks.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These benchmarks are meant as guidelines, as references.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: When insurers refer to these benchmarks, it is not something that prevents them from treating each claim on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Depending on the merits of the case and, certainly, if it is within the appropriate guidelines, insurers, I am sure, would continue to be able to fulfil their obligations to their policyholders, in accordance with the terms of their insurance products.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Going back to the earlier point that Dr Lim Wee Kiak raised with regard to the concern that some doctors may, as a result of this, raise their fees.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: The question is: how do you select the patients?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Because it is not really organised as a body.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We also have groups that can represent different stakeholders.
